Method of Attack: Impersonation of official MSI Afterburner download portals to distribute cryptocurrency miners and RedLine information-stealing malware
Dropping and running RedLine malware and XMR (Monero) miner via fake MSI Afterburner setup file
Using shellcode to retrieve XMR miner from GitHub and inject it into explorer.exe process memory
Miner mines Monero cryptocurrency stealthily after 60 minutes of CPU idling
Miner uses arguments to hide mining activity from process monitors and antivirus tools
RedLine malware steals passwords, cookies, browser information, and cryptocurrency wallets
Impacted Systems: Windows gamers and power users with powerful GPUs
Attack Vector: Fake MSI Afterburner download websites impersonating official site
Direct messages, forums, and social media posts promoting malicious domains
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious domains: msi-afterburner--download.site, msi-afterburner-download.site, msi-afterburner-download.tech, msi-afterburner-download.online, msi-afterburner-download.store, msi-afterburner-download.ru, msi-afterburner.download, mslafterburners.com, msi-afterburnerr.com
Non-MSI resembling domains promoted via direct messages and social media: git.git.skblxin.matrizauto.net and its subdomains
Hidden mining arguments: 'CPU max threads' set to 20, '-cinit-stealth-targets' to hide from Taskmgr.exe, ProcessHacker.exe, perfmon.exe, procexp.exe, procexp64.exe
Low antivirus detection rates on VirusTotal for MSIAfterburnerSetup.msi (3/56) and browser_assistant.exe (2/67)
